readings.title: The Ancient Egyptians
paragraphs: The ancient Egyptians lived in Egypt over five thousand years ago. They built their civilization along the Nile River. The river gave them water and food.
The Egyptians were famous for building pyramids. These giant structures were tombs for their kings, called pharaohs. The biggest pyramid is the Great Pyramid of Giza.

They also invented a writing system called hieroglyphics. It used pictures instead of letters. Scientists worked for many years to understand this ancient language. Today we can still see their amazing pyramids in Egypt.

readings.title: The Roman Empire
paragraphs: The Roman Empire was one of the most powerful empires in history. It started in Italy and grew to cover much of Europe, Africa, and Asia.
Romans built many things that we still use today. They made roads, bridges, and aqueducts to carry water. Their buildings were very strong and beautiful.
The Roman army was very organized and powerful. Soldiers trained hard and worked together as a team. This helped Rome win many battles. The Roman Empire fell in the year 476, but its legacy lives on.

readings.title: Christopher Columbus
paragraphs: Christopher Columbus was an explorer from Italy. In 1492, he sailed across the Atlantic Ocean with three ships. He wanted to find a new route to Asia.
Columbus never reached Asia. Instead, he arrived on an island in the Caribbean. He called the people there Indians because he thought he was in India.
His journey changed the world. It connected Europe and America for the first time. After Columbus, many more explorers sailed to the new continent. His voyage was brave and changed history forever.

readings.title: The Vikings
paragraphs: The Vikings were people from Scandinavia, in northern Europe. They lived over a thousand years ago. They were famous for being great sailors and warriors.
Viking ships were fast and strong. They could sail across the open sea and also travel up rivers. The front of their ships often had a dragon head.
The Vikings explored many lands. They reached Iceland, Greenland, and even North America. They also traded goods like furs, swords, and jewelry. Today we still find Viking treasures in the ground.

readings.title: Ancient Greece and the Olympics
paragraphs: Ancient Greece was home to many great thinkers and artists. The Greeks gave the world important ideas about science, math, and democracy.
The Olympic Games began in Greece over two thousand years ago. Athletes competed in sports like running, wrestling, and jumping. The games were held every four years.
Only men could compete in the ancient Olympics. Women had their own separate festival. Today, the Olympics include athletes from all over the world. The Olympic flame is still lit today in Greece.

readings.title: The Great Wall of China
paragraphs: The Great Wall of China is one of the most famous buildings in the world. It is over twenty-one thousand kilometers long. It was built to protect China from enemies.
Many different emperors built parts of the wall over hundreds of years. Workers used stone, brick, and earth to make it strong. Millions of people helped build it.
Today, the Great Wall is a popular place for tourists. People come from all over the world to walk along it. Some parts are very old, but others have been repaired.

readings.title: The Aztecs
paragraphs: The Aztecs were a powerful people who lived in Mexico. Their empire began in the 1300s. They built their capital city on an island in a lake.
The Aztecs were great farmers and builders. They grew corn, beans, and tomatoes. They also built beautiful temples and pyramids in their cities.

The Aztec empire ended when Spanish explorers arrived in 1519. The leader of the Aztecs was named Moctezuma. The Spanish brought new weapons and diseases. Today you can still see Aztec ruins in Mexico City.

readings.title: The Industrial Revolution
paragraphs: The Industrial Revolution began in England in the 1700s. It was a time when machines started to do work that people had done by hand.
Factories were built to make products like clothes and tools. Steam engines powered trains and ships. This made travel and trade much faster.

Life changed a lot for ordinary people. Many moved from farms to cities to work in factories. Children also worked in factories, which was very hard. Today machines do even more work in our modern world.

readings.title: World War II
paragraphs: World War II was a big war that lasted from 1939 to 1945. Many countries around the world were involved. It was the largest war in history.
The war was fought between two groups of countries. One group was called the Allies. The other group was called the Axis powers.

The war ended when the Allies won. After the war, countries worked together to build peace. They created the United Nations to help prevent future wars. It was a terrible time, but also a time of great courage.

readings.title: The Space Race
paragraphs: The Space Race was a competition between the United States and the Soviet Union. Both countries wanted to explore space first.
In 1961, a Soviet astronaut named Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. He orbited the Earth once and returned safely.

In 1969, the United States sent astronauts to the Moon. Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon. He said it was a giant leap for mankind. Today space exploration continues with new rockets and missions.
